metaDescription: Six 4 inch wood chippers compared by engine, blade and hammer design, chute, mobility and the PTO option, for yards, acreage and storm cleanup.
expertTake: The BILT HARD 274cc is the best overall because a 9 HP class engine, two blades plus four hammers and a stand and tow bar suit real branch cleanup on a property with trees. The SuperHandy 9HP is the value pick for steady pruning waste. If you only trim shrubs and small prunings, a corded electric shredder is easier and cheaper, and if you own a tractor with a PTO, the PTO chipper is the better route.
introParagraphs: A wood chipper feeds branches into a rotor with blades that slice the wood into chips, and the largest branch it can take is set by the feed opening, rotor and engine together. The number printed on the box is a ceiling, not a comfortable working size.

This guide explains how blades, hammers and engine power interact, why the feed rate matters as much as capacity, and how engine-driven and tractor-driven machines differ. Use the picks above for a shortlist, then read the reviews below for the tradeoffs on each machine.

products.name: BILT HARD 9 HP 274cc 4 Inch Gas Wood Chipper
products.description:
The BILT HARD pairs two chipping blades with four hammers, which means it chips branches and then shreds the leafy material that clogs simpler machines. The engine is a 274cc OHV four-stroke rated at 6.0 kW net at 3,600 RPM, and the net figure is worth noting because it is lower than the gross horsepower numbers on many boxes.

A 1.32 gallon fuel tank gives a useful working time, and two 10 inch solid wheels never go flat. A tow bar and a support stand let you move it and keep it stable while feeding. An adjustable discharge guide directs chips into a pile or bin.

Compared with the EFCUT C40E, it shares engine size but lacks the electric start. Change oil each season and sharpen or replace blades when chips look torn.
products.bestFor: Properties with regular branch cleanup that need a durable chipper and shredder.
pros: Blades plus hammers handle both wood and leafy debris
6.0 kW net rating is stated honestly
Solid wheels never go flat
Support stand improves stability while feeding
cons: Recoil start is harder in cold weather
Heavy to move without a towing vehicle

products.name: EFCUT C40E 4 Inch Electric Start Wood Chipper, 9HP 274cc
products.description:
The C40E adds a key-turn electric start to a 9HP 274cc engine, which matters on cold mornings when a recoil cord on a heavy flywheel is hard to pull. It also uses a larger flywheel at 15.9 inches, and a heavier flywheel stores energy that carries the rotor through a tough branch.

EFCUT claims a 15:1 reduction ratio, meaning fifteen piles of brush become one pile of chips, a figure that varies with material. Blades are made of high-speed steel and are longer than on some rivals.

Compared with the BILT HARD, it is an equal engine size with easier starting. The brand is newer, so check parts availability. Keep the battery charged and change oil seasonally.
products.bestFor: Owners who dislike recoil starting and want a 9 HP class chipper.
pros: Electric start removes the recoil cord struggle
Larger flywheel carries momentum through tough branches
High-speed steel blades hold an edge
15:1 reduction ratio claim cuts brush volume
cons: Battery adds a part to maintain
Reduction ratio depends on the material
Newer brand with less established parts support

products.name: SuperHandy 9HP 4 Inch Gas Wood Chipper with Reversible Blades
products.description:
SuperHandy offers a 9HP gas chipper with reversible dual-edge blades, which double the cutting life before replacement, since you flip them when one edge dulls. A vertically adjustable chute with a 110 degree range lets you aim chips into a bucket, tarp or bin.

It is a three-in-one that chips branches, shreds brush and mulches leaves. Compared with the BILT HARD's two blades plus four hammers, it uses a compact rotor, which is simpler and cheaper but less capable on leafy material.

Ownership is routine: oil changes, fresh fuel and blade flipping or sharpening. It suits home gardens and small farms.
products.bestFor: Home gardens and small farms that want an affordable 9 HP chipper.
pros: Reversible blades double cutting life
Chute adjusts 110 degrees for precise chip placement
Handles branches, brush and leaves
9HP engine suits steady pruning waste
cons: Compact rotor is less capable on leafy debris

products.name: MechMaxx 4 Inch Wood Chipper with 212cc 7HP Engine and Tow Bar
products.description:
MechMaxx uses a 212cc 7HP engine, a step below the 9 HP machines in this lineup, so it chips the same 4 inch limit more slowly. Two double-edge alloy steel blades work against an anvil, a classic chipper design that gives clean chips.

Two 14 inch wheels and a trailer bar make it easy to tow, and a 360 degree rotary discharge sends chips where you want them. An emergency stop button placed next to the feed port is close to the operator, which is a genuine safety advantage when something goes wrong.

Compared with the Honda-powered MechMaxx, it trades a recognized engine brand for a bigger displacement. Check parts support for the engine.
products.bestFor: Occasional branch cleanup where an emergency stop near the feed port matters.
pros: Emergency stop sits next to the feed port
360 degree discharge chute places chips freely
Large 14 in wheels roll over rough ground
Double-edge alloy blades work against an anvil
cons: 7HP engine chips slower than 9 HP rivals
Engine brand is less established for parts

products.name: MechMaxx 4 Inch Honda 196cc 6.5HP Towable Wood Chipper
products.description:
This MechMaxx has the same chassis as the 212cc model but swaps in a Honda 196cc 6.5HP engine. Honda engines are known for starting reliability and wide parts and service availability, which matters on a machine that sits for months between jobs.

Power is lower than the 7HP DUCAR and the 9 HP machines, so it works best on branches well under 4 inches and on steady feeding. The cutting system, emergency stop and 360 degree chute are the same.

Compared with the BILT HARD's 9 HP class engine, it is slower but easier to keep running for decades. Change oil each season and keep the air filter clean.
products.bestFor: Owners who prize engine reliability and parts support over raw chipping speed.
pros: Honda engine is known for easy starting and parts support
Emergency stop near the feed port
360 degree discharge places chips freely
Large 14 in wheels roll over rough ground
cons: 6.5HP is the lowest power in this gas group
Slower on branches near the 4 in limit

products.name: MechMaxx BX42S 4 Inch PTO 3-Point Wood Chipper
products.description:
This is a different kind of chipper: it has no engine and runs from a tractor's PTO, with a 3-point hitch mount. The tractor provides power far above a 9 HP engine, so the rotor carries steady momentum through wood without bogging.

A 26 inch rotor with four hardened steel blades and a self-feeding hopper pulls branches in, so you do not have to push. Rotor winglets create airflow that throws chips out. A 360 degree discharge chute adjusts direction.

It makes sense only if you already own a tractor, and the listing recommends tractors up to 45HP. Compared with the engine-driven models, there is no engine to maintain, but you need the tractor. Keep the PTO shaft greased.
products.bestFor: Property owners with a compact tractor who want engine-free, high-throughput chipping.
pros: Tractor PTO supplies far more power than a small engine
Self-feeding hopper pulls branches in
26 in rotor with four hardened blades chips fast
No separate engine to maintain
cons: Requires a tractor with a PTO and a 3-point hitch
Heavier and costlier than engine-driven chippers

buyingCriteria.explanation: A chipper at the 4 inch limit needs about 7 to 9 horsepower to keep the rotor spinning when it hits a dense branch. A smaller engine bogs and chips slowly. Gross horsepower on a box is higher than net, so look for net kW when it is stated. The BILT HARD lists 6.0 kW net, the EFCUT and SuperHandy 9HP, the MechMaxx DUCAR 7HP and the Honda unit 6.5HP.

Blades slice wood against an anvil, while hammers pound and shred leafy material. Blades-only machines clog on leafy brush, and hammers help them cope. The BILT HARD has two blades and four hammers, the MechMaxx gas models two blades and an anvil, and the SuperHandy has reversible dual-edge blades.

A heavy flywheel or rotor stores energy, carrying the cutters through dense wood. A light rotor stalls when the branch is hard. The EFCUT has a 15.9 inch flywheel, and the PTO chipper has a 26 inch rotor.
Recoil starting on a large single-cylinder engine is hard in cold weather. Electric start is easier but adds a battery. The EFCUT C40E has electric start, and the others use recoil.

Chippers are among the more dangerous yard machines. An emergency stop near the feed port, a stable stand and a long feed chute reduce risk. Never feed branches by hand into the rotor. The MechMaxx gas models place an emergency stop next to the feed port.
A chipper must be moved to the pile. Wheels, a tow bar and a stand matter. The MechMaxx has 14 inch wheels, the BILT HARD 10 inch solid wheels, and the PTO unit needs a tractor.

specDecoder.meaning: Gross horsepower is measured without accessories, and net is measured as installed. Net is lower and more honest.
specDecoder.watchFor: The BILT HARD states 6.0 kW net for its 274cc engine, which is about 8 HP.

specDecoder.meaning: The largest branch the feed opening and rotor can chip.
specDecoder.watchFor: A 4 inch limit is a ceiling for straight, green wood, and dense hardwood chips more slowly.

specDecoder.meaning: How much volume the chipper reduces, such as 15:1.
specDecoder.watchFor: The EFCUT claims 15:1, and the ratio depends on the material.

specDecoder.meaning: Power take-off, a rotating shaft on a tractor that drives implements.
specDecoder.watchFor: The MechMaxx BX42S needs a tractor and a suitable shaft.

specDecoder.meaning: Dual-edge blades that you flip when one edge dulls.
specDecoder.watchFor: They double blade life, but must be flipped correctly and torqued.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power and cutting
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared engine power and cutting system. The BILT HARD's 6.0 kW net and the 9HP engines led, and the Honda 6.5HP trailed.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety design
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared emergency stops, stands and feed designs. The MechMaxx emergency stop near the feed port scored well.

howWeEvaluated.title: Starting and ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered starting systems and parts support. The EFCUT's electric start and the Honda's parts support led.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mobility
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared wheels, tow bars and stands. The MechMaxx 14 inch wheels and BILT HARD stand scored well.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We read patterns in owner feedback on clogging, blade wear and starting. Where specs and feedback disagreed, we weighted the feedback.

howToChoose.intro: The debris sets the cutting system.

cards.label: Engine-driven
cards.text: Self-contained and portable, but limited by engine size and upkeep. The BILT HARD, EFCUT, SuperHandy and both MechMaxx gas models fall here.

cards.label: PTO-driven
cards.text: Powered by a tractor, so there is no engine to maintain and plenty of power, but it requires a tractor. The MechMaxx BX42S falls here.

howToChoose.note: Choose engine-driven for portability, and PTO if you already own a suitable tractor.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A strong engine, a heavy rotor and a stable stand. Storm debris is mixed and often green, so clogging resistance matters.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The BILT HARD's blades and hammers and the EFCUT's heavy flywheel suit mixed debris, and the PTO unit is best on large acreage.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You chip often or process leafy brush. The BILT HARD gives hammers and a stand, and the EFCUT gives electric start.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You chip a few times a year. The MechMaxx 212cc or SuperHandy does the job.

maintenance.why: Oil breaks down and protects the engine. Fresh oil extends engine life.
Dull blades tear wood and strain the engine. Sharp blades make clean chips.
Vibration loosens bolts. A loose blade is a serious hazard.
Gasoline varnishes carburetors. Stabilizer or draining prevents hard starts.

maintenance.task: Clean the chute and rotor housing
maintenance.why: Packed chips cause clogging and rust. Clear them with the engine off.

faq.q: Can a 4 inch chipper really chip 4 inch branches?
faq.a: Yes, but slowly if they are dense hardwood. Straight, green branches under 3 inches chip comfortably.
Smaller engines cost less, and 9 HP machines with hammers or electric start cost more. Consider the debris you process.

faq.q: How much engine do I need?
faq.a: About 7 to 9 horsepower for a 4 inch limit. Smaller engines bog on dense wood.
Only if recoil starting is hard for you, especially in cold weather.
If you own a compact tractor, yes, because it avoids engine upkeep. Otherwise it is not an option.
Wear eye and ear protection, gloves and snug clothing. Never reach into the feed chute, feed butt end first, and shut off the engine before clearing jams.
